problems.title: Aileron torque tube with a touch point
problems.setup: An aileron torque tube is clamped at a wing rib at x = 0 and loaded by a hinge torque T at its outboard end x = 1.6 m. Inboard segment (0 to 0.8 m): thin aluminium tube, mean radius 25 mm, wall 2 mm. Outboard segment (0.8 to 1.6 m): mean radius 20 mm, wall 1.5 mm. G = 27 GPa. A lug at the junction x = 0.8 m sits 1.0° away from a rigid stop, so the junction rotates 1.0° and then touches.

parts.ask: Tip torsional stiffness T/φ_tip before the lug touches
sol: Thin circular tube: J = 2πr³t (r/t = 12.5 and 13.3, thin wall holds)
J₁ = 1.963×10⁻⁷ m⁴, k₁ = GJ₁/L₁ = 6627 N·m/rad
J₂ = 7.540×10⁻⁸ m⁴, k₂ = GJ₂/L₂ = 2545 N·m/rad
Same torque in both segments, twists add: series, 1/k = 1/k₁ + 1/k₂
k = 1839 N·m/rad

parts.ask: Tip torque T_c at which the lug touches the stop
sol: Only the inboard segment lies between the root and the junction: φ_junction = T/k₁
Touch when T/k₁ = 1.0° = 0.01745 rad

parts.ask: Tip twist at T = 200 N·m
sol: The junction stays at 1.0° once it rests on the stop
The outboard segment always carries the full T: T/k₂ = 200/2545 = 0.0786 rad = 4.50°

parts.ask: Above T_c, what carries the extra torque and what is the tip stiffness?
parts.a: The stop carries T − T_c, the inboard segment stays at T_c, and the tip stiffness rises to k₂ = 2545 N·m/rad
w: Both segments keep acting in series, so the tip stiffness stays at 1839 N·m/rad
The stop acts in series with the inboard segment, so the tip stiffness falls below 1839 N·m/rad
The stop adds in parallel with the outboard segment, so the tip stiffness becomes k₁ + k₂
sol: The stop is a parallel path from the junction to ground, and a rigid one fixes the junction
A cut through the outboard segment shows it carries T at every load: tip piece equilibrium
The torque-twist curve is piecewise linear with a stiffer second branch

parts.ask: Twist: the stop is a rubber bumper with k_b = 4000 N·m/rad once touched. Tip twist at T = 200 N·m
sol: After touch the bumper and the inboard segment act in parallel at the junction: k₁ + k_b = 10 627 N·m/rad
Tip: add the outboard 4.503°, φ_tip = 5.96°

problems.x: Torsion segments along a span act as springs in series, and a touch point adds a parallel path to ground at its node, which raises the stiffness seen at that node and everywhere outboard of it.

problems.title: Three-rod hanger by TSTP and TMTP
problems.setup: A lander mockup of weight P = 30 kN hangs from a test gantry on three steel rods that meet at joint D. The centre rod is vertical with length L = 1 m; the two outer rods are at 45° to it, length √2 m. Every rod has EA = 20 MN. TSTP: total potential with displacements as unknowns. TMTP: total complementary potential with member forces as unknowns.

parts.ask: Which statement describes the two principles?
parts.a: TSTP: assume compatible displacements, and stationarity gives equilibrium. TMTP: assume forces in equilibrium with P, and stationarity gives compatibility
w: TSTP: assume forces in equilibrium, and stationarity gives compatibility. TMTP: assume compatible displacements, and stationarity gives equilibrium
Both assume equilibrium; they differ only by the sign of the load term
TSTP needs a redundant force as its unknown and TMTP needs the joint displacement
sol: Π(u) = U(u) − Pu over kinematically admissible u
Π*(N) = U*(N) − (work of prescribed support displacements) over statically admissible N
For a linear elastic truss both give the exact answer

parts.ask: TSTP with the joint drop u as the one unknown (symmetry): u
sol: Each outer rod stretches u cos 45° = u/√2
Π = ½(EA/L)u² + 2·½(EA/(√2L))(u/√2)² − Pu = ½(EA/L)(1 + 1/√2)u² − Pu

parts.ask: TMTP with the centre rod force X as the redundant: X
sol: Joint equilibrium: each outer rod carries (P − X)/√2
Check: XL/EA = 0.879 mm, the same u

parts.ask: A rushed TMTP guess sets X = P/2 without minimising. Estimate u from u = 2Π*/P with that X
sol: 3% above 0.879 mm: an equilibrium guess overestimates flexibility, a displacement guess underestimates it

parts.ask: Twist: the mockup is removed, a jack pushes joint D straight up with P = 30 kN, and the two outer rods are swapped for cables. Joint rise u?
sol: An upward P would put all three members in compression
Cables carry tension only, so the outer cables go slack
The centre rod takes all of P as a strut: u = PL/EA = 1.5 mm (then check it for buckling)

problems.x: TSTP builds compatibility in and returns equilibrium, TMTP builds equilibrium in and returns compatibility, and both give the exact answer for a linear elastic truss.

problems.title: Three-segment boom: antisymmetric mode and a sudden preload
problems.setup: A folding boom is modelled as three rigid segments AB, BC and CD, each L = 0.5 m, pinned at A, with D on a roller along the axis. Joints B and C each have a lateral spring k = 60 kN/m that stays perpendicular to the axis. A compressive dead load P acts along the axis at D. y_B and y_C are lateral joint displacements from the straight axis, and equal lumped masses sit at B and C.

parts.ask: Total potential Π(y_B, y_C) for small displacements:
w: Π = ½k(y_B² + y_C²) − (P/(2L))(y_B² + y_C²)
Π = ½k(y_B² + y_C²) + (P/L)(y_B² − y_By_C + y_C²)
Π = ½k(y_B² + y_C²) − (P/L)(y_B² + y_By_C + y_C²)
sol: Each segment shortens the span by (Δy)²/(2L)
Shortening = (1/(2L))[y_B² + (y_C − y_B)² + y_C²] = (1/L)(y_B² − y_By_C + y_C²)
The dead load loses potential P times that shortening

parts.ask: Critical load P_cr
sol: Hessian: [[k − 2P/L, P/L],[P/L, k − 2P/L]]
y_B = y_C: k − P/L = 0, P = kL = 30 kN
y_B = −y_C: k − 3P/L = 0, P = kL/3 = 10 kN
The lowest root governs: P_cr = 10 kN

parts.ask: Which buckled shape goes with P_cr?
parts.a: The antisymmetric S shape: y_C = −y_B, with the middle segment rotating about the boom centre
w: The symmetric bow: y_B = y_C, with the middle segment translating sideways
Only B moves while C stays on the axis
Both shapes together, since the two springs are equal
sol: For the same spring energy ky², the S shape shortens the span by 3y²/L and the bow by y²/L
More load travel per unit of spring energy means a lower critical load

parts.ask: The as-built boom has y_B = −y_C = 2 mm with the springs unstretched there. A latch applies P = 6 kN suddenly and holds it. Peak |y_B| (linear, undamped)
sol: In the antisymmetric mode: equilibrium at y = y₀/(1 − P/P_cr) = 2/0.4 = 5 mm
A step load starts the joints at rest at 2 mm, so they oscillate about 5 mm
Peak = 2·5 − 2 = 8 mm: twice the static increment

parts.ask: Twist: the hinges allow |y_B| up to 6 mm. Largest preload if applied suddenly (slowly it would be 6.67 kN)?
sol: Sudden peak: y₀(1 + r)/(1 − r) with r = P/P_cr
Set equal to 3y₀: 1 + r = 3 − 3r, r = 0.5
P = 5 kN, against r = 2/3 (6.67 kN) for slow loading

problems.x: A three-segment spring chain buckles first in its antisymmetric mode at kL/3, and a step load doubles the deflection increment of a linear structure.

problems.title: Cross-braced tower bay by the unit load method
problems.setup: A test bay of a launch umbilical tower is a pin-jointed rectangle ABCD with A (0, 0), B (3, 0), C (3, 4), D (0, 4) in metres, and both diagonals AC and BD. A is pinned and B sits on a roller with a vertical reaction only. A horizontal wind load P = 60 kN acts at D in the +x direction. The four sides have EA = 200 MN and each diagonal has EA = 100 MN. Tension is positive.

parts.ask: Degree of static indeterminacy
sol: One redundant: cut one diagonal

parts.ask: Force in diagonal BD
sol: Release BD. System 0 (P only): AC +100, BC −80, CD −60, AB and DA carry zero
System 1 (unit tension pair in BD): AB, CD −0.6; BC, DA −0.8; AC +1
δ₁₀ = ΣN₀n₁L/EA = 0.00682 m, δ₁₁ = Σn₁²L/EA (BD included) = 1.364×10⁻⁷ m/N
δ₁₀ + Xδ₁₁ = 0: X = −50 kN, so BD is in compression

parts.ask: Horizontal deflection of D
sol: Final forces N = N₀ + Xn₁: AB +30, BC −40, CD −30, DA +40, AC +50, BD −50 kN
Unit load at D on the released structure: n = N₀/P
u_D = ΣNnL/EA = 5.68 mm

parts.ask: Why may the unit load for u_D sit on the released, determinate structure?
parts.a: The virtual force set only needs equilibrium with the unit load; the real forces N already satisfy compatibility, so any such set gives the same u_D
w: Because a unit load produces zero force in the redundant member
Because the released structure has the same stiffness as the real one
It is an approximation that holds when the redundant force is small
sol: Virtual force principle: 1·u_D = Σ n (NL/EA) for any n in equilibrium with the unit load
This is the reduction theorem: it saves a second indeterminate solution

parts.ask: Twist: the diagonals are thin tension-only rods. Horizontal deflection of D?
sol: BD would carry −50 kN, so a tension-only rod goes slack
AC alone braces the bay: the released system 0 forces now act, AC +100 kN in tension
u_D = ΣN₀²L/(P·EA) = 11.37 mm, twice the braced value

problems.x: The unit load method solves an indeterminate truss with one compatibility equation at the cut, δ₁₀ + Xδ₁₁ = 0, and the deflection unit load can sit on the released structure.

problems.title: Lunar lander camera mast: change the trial function
problems.setup: A camera mast on a lunar lander is a slender carbon tube clamped to the deck at x = 0 and free at the top x = L, carrying the camera head as a vertical dead load P. L = 2 m, EI = 2 kN·m². Use the Rayleigh quotient P = ∫EI(w″)² dx / ∫(w′)² dx. Exact: P_cr = π²EI/(4L²) = 1234 N.

parts.ask: Trial w = a x²: estimate of P_cr
sol: w″ = 2a, ∫EI(w″)² dx = 4EIa²L
w′ = 2ax, ∫(w′)² dx = 4a²L³/3
P = 3EI/L² = 1500 N, 21.6% high

parts.ask: Trial w = a(3Lx² − x³), the static tip-load shape: estimate of P_cr
sol: w″ = 6a(L − x), ∫EI(w″)² dx = 12EIa²L³
w′ = 3a(2Lx − x²), ∫(w′)² dx = 4.8a²L⁵
P = 2.5EI/L² = 1250 N, 1.3% high

parts.ask: Why does the cubic beat the parabola, and which way do both err?
parts.a: Both are upper bounds; the cubic also meets the natural tip condition EIw″(L) = 0, while the parabola keeps a constant curvature (a false tip moment) that adds stiffness
w: Both are lower bounds, and the cubic is closer simply because it has a higher power
The parabola violates the essential condition w′(0) = 0, which is why it is high
The cubic is exact for the column because it is the static deflection shape
sol: Admissible trial shapes meet w(0) = 0 and w′(0) = 0; both do
Any admissible shape constrains the column, so the Rayleigh quotient sits above P_cr
Meeting the natural conditions as well brings the estimate closer

parts.ask: Twist: the deck is soft, so the base becomes a rotational spring C = 1 kN·m/rad. Use w = a₁x + a₂x². Estimate of P_cr
sol: The base slope is now free (the spring is a natural condition): add ½C w′(0)² = ½Ca₁² to U
[[C − PL, −PL²],[−PL², 4EIL − 4PL³/3]] has zero determinant
Numbers: P² − 8000P + 3×10⁶ = 0, P = 394 N
Exact from kL tan kL = CL/EI = 1: kL = 0.860, P = 370 N, still below the Ritz value

problems.x: The Rayleigh quotient with an admissible trial shape gives an upper bound on P_cr, and a shape that also meets the natural conditions lands closest.

problems.title: Solar HALE wing: which load drives which mode
problems.setup: A solar HALE UAV wing is a uniform cantilever of semi-span L = 10 m clamped at the fuselage, with EI = 4×10⁵ N·m², GJ = 2×10⁵ N·m², mass m = 10 kg/m and torsional mass moment of inertia I_α = 0.5 kg·m²/m about the elastic axis. Uniform cantilever results: ω_n = (β_nL)²√(EI/(mL⁴)) with β₁L = 1.875 and β₂L = 4.694; first torsion ω_T = (π/(2L))√(GJ/I_α).

parts.ask: Boundary conditions as physical statements:
parts.a: Root: w = 0 and w′ = 0 (the fuselage holds deflection and slope), θ = 0. Tip: EIw″ = 0 and (EIw″)′ = 0 (a free end carries zero moment and zero shear), GJθ′ = 0
w: Root: w = 0 and EIw″ = 0. Tip: w′ = 0 and (EIw″)′ = 0
Root: w = 0 and w′ = 0. Tip: w = 0 and w′ = 0
Root: w = 0 and w′ = 0. Tip: w″ = 0 and θ = 0
sol: Clamp: two kinematic conditions on deflection and slope, and zero twist
Free end: two force conditions, M = EIw″ and V = (EIw″)′ vanish, and the torque GJθ′ vanishes

parts.ask: First bending frequency f₁
sol: f₁ = ω₁/(2π) = 1.12 Hz; second bending is (4.694/1.875)² = 6.27 times higher

parts.ask: First torsion frequency f_T
sol: f_T = 15.8 Hz: torsion is far stiffer than bending on this wing

parts.ask: A symmetric vertical gust adds lift through the elastic axis, and a deflected outboard aileron adds a pitching moment about it. Which modes do they mainly drive?
parts.a: The gust drives the bending modes, mostly the first; the aileron moment drives the torsion mode
w: The gust drives torsion and the aileron drives bending
Both drive only torsion, since both change the lift
Both drive only the second bending mode, since they act near the tip
sol: A load excites a mode in proportion to the work it does on that mode shape
Lift through the elastic axis does work on w, a moment about it does work on θ
An offset between the centre of mass, the aerodynamic centre and the elastic axis couples the two

parts.ask: Twist: a 50 kg battery pod is hung at each tip. Rayleigh estimate of the first bending frequency
sol: Use the static tip-load shape: k = 3EI/L³ = 1200 N/m
Effective mass: M + (33/140)mL = 50 + 23.6 = 73.6 kg

problems.x: A clamped root holds deflection and slope, a free tip carries zero moment and shear, and a load drives the mode whose shape it does work on.
